content:
Hi everyone! I formalized Napoleon's Theorem in Lean using Claude, but I'm not entirely sure if the result is truly idiomatic for Lean.

To be honest, I'm quite new to coding in Lean. While I have a strong mathematics background, writing code is still very new to me. The idea of formalizing theorems in Lean really excites me, which is why I decided to tackle one of my favorite theorems, Napoleon's Theorem, with the help of AI.

I would love it if experienced members could critique my code and my approach to using AI for this. I really want to learn where my blind spots are and what I might be doing wrong. I apologize in advance if my questions come across as very basic or naïve—I'm just really eager to learn.

You can find the repository here: https://github.com/imran-tanrikolu/Napoleon-s-Theorem-in-Lean4.git

Any feedback is highly appreciated. Thank you!

What do you mean by "is idiomatic"? You've decided to use complex numbers, you have defined IsEquilateral to mean an algebraic identity rather than the usual definition (and have not proved the equivalence) and then the result is basically a triviality.
What I can say is that you will not learn if you use AI.

Yes, that's another very good point: you are just one more user who has discovered that Claude can write lean and has pressed a button. This zulip is full of such people now and it's a big change. The only thing that has happened here is that a bunch of code that will never be used has been generated and the tech companies have got a bit more money (and that you joined the very long list of people who have discovered that this is possible)

It’s clear to me now that to truly learn Lean, I need to focus on studying the proper literature and tutorials to understand the core concepts myself rather than relying on AI shortcuts. Thank you for pointing this out
I think this topic belongs in #AI authored projects
This topic was moved here from #new members > Feedback requested: Napoleon's Theorem using Claude by Michael Rothgang.

@İmran Tanrikolu
I suppose it is not bad, that you have learned that Claude can do that. Its rather that most people here are somewhat annoyed, by people coming on the zulip and announcing it as if they just solved math and have made a huge discovery. You were a lot nicer than others, but the community is still a bit strained from previous discussions :)

If you want to learn more on Lean, you can look here. Also at the very least learn how to read / write (good) statements, proofs you can theoretically abstract away with AI, but you should still learn some basic proofing in lean, such as by working through MIL.
